A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CR-DAgger work. All main sections, Figures 1–8, Table 1, and Appendices A.1–A.5 are readable and matchable despite changed pagination.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original robot experiments on book flipping and belt assembly, supplemented by stage-wise results and a base-action-input ablation in Appendices A.1–A.2.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendices A.1–A.2 retain the authors' original robot evaluations and ablation results, including Figures 6–8 and Table 1.

M1.justification: Both retain the same compliant intervention interface, residual policy with force input and pose/wrench outputs, and training strategies in Sections 3.1–3.2 and Appendix A.3.

E1.justification: Both use book flipping and belt assembly with the same seen/unseen-book cases, shelf configurations, and pulley-board positions. No training or evaluation coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Section 4.3 and Figure 6 retain Observe-then-Collect and Take-over-Correction/HG-DAgger, alongside retraining, finetuning, and force-free residual comparisons. Comparator participation in each comparison is unchanged.

E3.justification: Both specify 150 base-policy demonstrations per task, 50 correction episodes per collection method, and 20 evaluation trials across four test cases. Model settings, controls, sampling procedures, and ablation protocols are unchanged.

E4.justification: The force-removal, training-frequency, sampling-strategy, and base-action-input ablations are retained unchanged. Failure examples and stage-wise analyses in Figures 4–5 and Appendix A.1 also match.

E5.justification: Both retain evaluation trial counts and point success rates. Neither reports training-seed repetitions, uncertainty intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Figures 6–8 and Table 1 contain identical result entries. CR with On-Policy Delta remains at 100% book-flipping and 70% belt-assembly success, versus base-policy rates of 40% and 20%. Qualitative findings also match.

T1.justification: The policy/action notation and mathematical specification in Figure 3 and Section 3.2 are unchanged. Neither version contains formal theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same two methodological contributions and claims about efficient policy improvement and superiority to retraining and finetuning.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning force feedback, correction smoothness, distribution shift, and training stability are identical. Section 5 retains the recommended 10–20% minimum base-policy success and the limitation concerning multimodal actions.

D1.justification: Implementation settings, correction-data handling, RTX 4090 compute information, and task-specific hardware details are unchanged. Both retain the same project link and promised hardware, training-data, and policy-code release.

R1.justification: The same 45 references and substantive related-work discussion are retained, including the positioning relative to human-intervention and residual-policy approaches.

P1.justification: The arXiv stamp changes from v1 dated 20 June 2025 to v2 dated 24 July 2025. Paper wording, headings, terminology, and section and appendix order are otherwise unchanged.

P2.justification: Vertical spacing and page breaks change, with acknowledgments spilling onto a mostly blank page 10 and references and appendices shifting one page later. Figures 1–8 and Table 1 retain their content, designs, and captions.

improvement.justification: The scientific content, results, limitations, and reproducibility information are unchanged, including all appendices. The spacing and pagination adjustments neither resolve a substantive deficiency nor materially harm readability or evidential support.
